description: The image displays two concentric pie charts comparing the distribution of educational content categories under two different classification systems: “AttentionInfluence” on the left and “FineWeb-Edu Classifier” on the right. Each chart is divided into multiple colored segments representing distinct topic areas, with numerical values indicating the count or weight of items in each category. In the “AttentionInfluence” chart, the largest segment is “Education” (25), followed by “History & Society” (23), “Health & Medicine” (22), and “Teaching & resources” (15). Smaller segments include “Science” (15), “Animal & Plant” (13), “Tech & Engineer” (12), “Diseases” (11), “Society & culture” (10), “Science & technology education” (10), “Historical review” (7), “Events & people” (6), “Nutrition” (5), “Infor tech” (5), “Materials” (3), “Fin & Law” (3), “Manage” (2), “Policy” (1), and “Emerging tech” (4). The “FineWeb-Edu Classifier” chart shows a different distribution, with “Education” as the largest segment (38), followed by “History & Society” (19), “Science & technology education” (19), “Health & Medicine” (19), “Teaching & resources” (17), “Science” (15), “Animal & Plant” (12), “Historical review” (12), “Tech & Engineer” (8), “Society & culture” (5), “Infor tech” (3), “Materials” (3), “Emerging tech” (4), “Manage” (1), “Healthy education” (2), “Diseases” (10), “Nutrition” (7), and “Medical” (2). Both charts use color-coding and labels with connecting lines to identify each segment, and the inner rings in both charts break down broader categories into subcategories. The visual comparison suggests that the “FineWeb-Edu Classifier” assigns higher weights to general “Education” and “History & Society” categories, while “AttentionInfluence” distributes emphasis more evenly across science, health, and technology-related domains.
